title: Interleaved evaluation crosswalk and judge-calibration protocol for config rollouts
creator: Sasha Martinez
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable protocol that links configuration changes (temperature, top_p, quantization, KV cache behavior) and model variant swaps to calibrated quality signals used by rollout gating and alerting.

Background: Current rollout checks use raw LLM-as-judge scores and ad-hoc cohorts. We see score drift across temperatures and quantized variants that produces false positives/negatives when gating. We need a crosswalk and calibration layer so the rollout system compares apples-to-apples and surfaces statistically meaningful regressions.

Scope:
- Define interleaved synthetic-control cohorts (anchor prompts + production cohorts) to run alongside any experimental config.
- Establish judge-calibration: run LLM-as-judge at multiple temperatures and map judge confidence to calibrated score percentiles per-cohort.
- Build a per-config calibration artifact: mapping table that converts judge raw score -> calibrated z-score and confidence interval for the given (model, temp, quantization) tuple.
- Integrate calibration into the evaluation pipeline so rollouts and automatic canaries compare calibrated metrics and trigger alerts only for statistically significant regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- We can produce a calibration artifact within 30 minutes for a new (model, temp, quant) combination on the eval infra.
- Rollout gating rules using calibrated metrics reduce false positive alerts by >40% on historical 6-week dataset (retrospective test).
- Per-cohort delta detection achieves >95% precision at detecting simulated degradations >= 3% absolute in the primary cohort metric.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec and rubric: PM drafts a "crosswalk spec" that describes cohorts, synthetic anchors, judge temperature sweep, and statistical tests (bootstrap CIs, Benjamini-Hochberg for multiple cohorts). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/Crosswalk+Spec (working draft).
2) Data collection: ENG builds interleaved runner to sample traffic and inject synthetic anchor prompts, record raw judge outputs at temp=[0.0,0.2,0.6,1.0].
3) Calibration model: Research provides mapping code (isotonic regression + temperature-aware scaling) that produces calibration.artifact.json (flat table).
4) Integration: Console shows per-config calibrated metrics, CI bands, and gating decision. Rollout engine consumes artifacts to compute z-scores.
5) Canary and retrospective test: Run closed retrospective on last 6 weeks and a live canary for next dedicated rollout.

Risks & mitigations:
- Judge instability across temps: mitigate by using ensemble of judge prompts (3 paraphrases) and median aggregation.
- Compute cost of temperature sweep: only sweep on candidate configs and use cached artifacts for minor param changes.
- False sense of safety if cohorts miss edge cases: maintain human-in-the-loop review for P0 rollouts and periodic adversarial sweeps.

Deliverables:
- Crosswalk spec (Confluence)
- Calibration artifact generator (python tool, ENG PR)
- Pipeline job that produces artifacts and uploads to artifact store
- Console UI tiles for calibrated metrics and gating status
- Retrospective report comparing current gating to calibrated gating

Notes on scope exclusions: This ticket does not include building a new judge model or changing existing rubric categories — it focuses on calibration and crosswalk for current judge rubric. Changes to the rubric itself will be tracked separately.
